items.title: The selected Gaussian surface integral

source.anchor: B.7 proof A2.SS2.SSS2.p4.5 uniform Oe1 sentence; A.1 proof A1.SS1.p2.1 normalized surface convention; Eq21-23 for selected transport
source.attribution: Huanjian Zhou and Taiji Suzuki, On Complexity of Gaussian Sampling. ASTIS expands the standard surface-law identification used by the source. Shared background is explicitly generalized to every existing coordinate and positive finite dimension.
source.scope: Identify actual full-Haar first-column law with actual normalized volume-derived sphere probability, and transport existing absolute selected-kernel L1 and actual signed Gaussian integral to that same canonical surface law. Neither Poisson value, evaluated Eq24, actual positive TV ratio, amplification/oracle/query/cost, hidden-eigenbasis or main theorem is asserted. Surface normalization/invariance, any invariant-law uniqueness/transitivity and all measurability are proof dependencies, never new public premises.

items.statement: For natural \(n\ge3\) and real \(\kappa\ge4\), use the literal selected \(s,r,\ell,\beta\), actual precision \(A_O\), Gaussian \(\gamma_O\), signed expectation \(H_\gamma(\ell)\), and kernel \(f\) defined below. Let \(\nu=(O\mapsto Oe_1)_*\mu\) for actual normalized full orthogonal Haar. Let \(\tau=\mathrm{vol}.\mathrm{toSphere}\) on the actual Euclidean unit sphere, and \(\sigma=\tau(S)^{-1}\iota_*\tau\). Then \(\nu=\sigma\), \(\sigma\) is a probability, \(f\in L^1(\sigma)\), and \(H_\gamma(\ell)=\beta\int f\,d\sigma\). The parameters are \(s=\sqrt\kappa\), \(r=(1-1/n)(s-1)/(s+1)\), \(\ell=(4ns+(s-1)^2)/(8n(n-1))\), \(\beta=(-1)^{n-1}(s-1)^{n-1}(1-1/n)^{n/2}/(s+1)^n\). Here \(f(y)=((s+1)y_1-(s-1))/(1+r^2-2ry_1)^{n/2}\), \(A_O=((\kappa+1)/2)I-((\kappa-1)/4)(O+O^\top)\), \(\gamma_O=\mathcal N(0,A_O^{-1})\), and \(H_\gamma(\ell)=\mathbb E_\mu[\det(O)\int e^{-\ell\|x\|_2^2}\,d\gamma_O]\). Real \(n/2\) powers are retained. Neither Poisson value nor evaluated Eq24 is asserted.
assumptions: Exactly \(n\in\mathbb N,\ n\ge3\) and \(\kappa\in\mathbb R,\ \kappa\ge4\), including \(\kappa=4\). All parameter divisions are real, and \(n/2\) is a real exponent even for odd dimensions.
\(\mu\) is the existing actual normalized Haar probability on full \(O(n)\), including reflections. \(c(O)=Oe_1\) uses the Euclidean l2 norm, and \(\nu=c_*\mu\) is its literal ambient pushforward.

\(\sigma\) is the literal normalized Euclidean volume-derived surface measure. Its equality with the actual Haar first-column law, its probability normalization, and \(f\in L^1(\sigma)\) are conclusions, with no additional public premises. The ambient quotient retains standard totalized real division/rpow; no off-sphere positivity or continuity is asserted.
